CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sarah is a 27-year-old female presenting for her annual visit. She reports that she has been struggling with depression, which has worsened over the past year due to being isolated indoors and working remotely. She is currently taking Prozac 20mg daily, which has helped her in the past. She states that a lot has been weighing on her lately. She also reports chronic back pain that is managed but exacerbated by prolonged sitting at her desk at work. The pain improves with movement and positional changes. She denies tingling or radiating leg pain but reports some numbness in her legs that feels like the limb is "falling asleep." Symptoms improve with standing or changing position. She denies weakness in her legs. She is able to perform activities of daily living including exercising and going to the store, though she is bothered by extremes of prolonged sitting or standing. She has a history of congenital coronary artery disease for which she underwent coronary artery bypass grafting at a young age. She reports her heart has been doing well with good arterial function.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for depression and chronic back pain. Positive for some leg numbness. Negative for leg tingling, leg pain, or leg weakness. Otherwise unremarkable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Coronary artery disease s/p coronary artery bypass grafting (congenital)
Chronic back pain
Depression

MEDICATIONS
Prozac 20mg daily (to be increased to 40mg daily)
Aspirin 81mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works at desk job, remote work arrangement. Exercises regularly. Able to go to store and perform activities of daily living.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Does not appear in distress
Neck: No thyroid enlargement
Cardiovascular: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur, stable
Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally
Abdomen: Soft
Musculoskeletal: Pain on palpation of lumbar spine, decreased flexion of back
Neurological: Lower extremity strength intact
Extremities: No edema

RESULTS
ECG: Basically unchanged from last year
Lumbar spine X-ray: Stable compared to last year

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Depression: Increase Prozac from 20mg to 40mg daily (one tablet once daily). Prescription to be sent to pharmacy.
2. Chronic back pain: Refer to physical therapy. Patient declines pain medication at this time and prefers to start with physical therapy.
3. Coronary artery disease s/p CABG: Order echocardiogram. Continue aspirin 81mg daily.
4. Patient to follow up with nurse to schedule appointments for physical therapy and echocardiogram.
